title: Golden calf
def: The calf the Israelites worshipped while Moses was on the mountain; in the Quran it was made by al-Samiri, not by Aaron.
what: The Quran says that after Moses left, his people took “a calf, a body with a lowing sound”, made of their ornaments (7:148, 20:88). It names al-Samiri as the one who led them to it (20:85, 20:95–97). Aaron warned them that they were being tested and told them to follow him (20:90). Moses rebuked the people and al-Samiri, burned the calf and scattered it in the sea (20:97).
sources: In the Quran it is Aaron who opposes the calf, and Moses’ anger at him (7:150) is that of a brother who feared he had not done enough. The Quran uses the story as an example of the Israelites’ readiness to fall back into idolatry, and of forgiveness after repentance (2:54).

title: Greed and avarice
def: The Quran condemns miserliness and hoarding, and promises success to those saved from the greed of their own souls.
what: “Those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty should not think it good for them; it will be a burden on their necks on the Day of Resurrection” (3:180). Of those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in God’s way, the Quran promises a painful punishment (9:34). “Whoever is saved from the greed of his own soul, those are the successful” (59:9).
